summary: FinCEN penalty against Bank of America

claims.text: FinCEN imposed a $1.2 billion penalty on Bank of America for systemic failures in its BSA/AML program, specifically for failing to mitigate priority national security risks such as Chinese money laundering networks and illicit finance activities along the U.S. southwest border. The enforcement action stems from the bank’s willful violations of the BSA and its failure to maintain an effective AML program, including inadequate due diligence on foreign correspondent accounts and insufficient Suspicious Activity Report filings.

evidence.quote: Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) announced that it has assessed a $1.2 billion penalty against Bank of America, N.A.
(Bank of America) for its failure to mitigate and report priority national security risks, including Chinese money laundering networks and illicit finance along the southwest border.

As part of its resolution with FinCEN, Bank of America admits that it willfully violated the BSA and failed to implement and maintain an AML program that met the minimum requirements of the BSA and FinCEN’s implementing regulations, conduct due diligence for correspondent accounts for foreign financial institutions, and file Suspicious Activity Reports.

claims.text: Concurrently, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency assessed a $750 million civil money penalty for the bank’s deficient BSA/AML compliance program, while the Office of Foreign Assets Control reached an $11.6 million settlement over apparent violations of sanctions programs targeting Iran, Russia, narcotics trafficking, and global terrorism. These actions reflect multiple regulatory concerns across compliance, sanctions, and national security risk management.

evidence.quote: Concurrently, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency assessed a $750 million civil money penalty for the bank’s deficient and ineffective Bank Secrecy Act/anti-money laundering (BSA/AML) compliance program.

In addition, the Office of Foreign Assets Control announced an $11.6 million settlement agreement with the bank over apparent violations of numerous sanctions programs, including on Iran, Russia, narcotics, and global terrorism.

implications.text: The scale of the penalty and the admission of willful BSA violations may signal heightened regulatory scrutiny on large banks’ ability to detect and report national security-related financial risks, particularly those involving foreign jurisdictions and cross-border correspondent relationships.
